paper_read.note: Four-page covering report (28278) whose figures all sit in Appendix 1 (28279, 23pp). Read from the appendix. Report author 'Claire Hobley / Louise Allison' dated June 2026; lead officer is the Director: Transformation and Outcomes (name not printed). No email addresses in either document — the front sheet lists a postal address (Church Square House, Scunthorpe DN15 6NL) but no direct dials or emails. Adviser is Link Group (glossary calls it 'MUFG Corporate Markets'). Book is wholly fixed-rate — no LOBOs. Reconciliation is exceptionally clean: 44 PWLB loans / £138,905,254 / 3.9227% weighted (our engine at 2026-03-31) exactly ties the paper's Appendix §3 p.7 debt-portfolio table figure of £138.9m PWLB at 3.92%. Balance-sheet identity ties to the pound. All five printed PWLB certainty rates at 31/3/26 (1y 5.04, 5y 5.28, 10y 5.72, 25y 6.29, 50y 6.08) agree with our series for the same day to the basis point — same set as Shropshire's Appendix A, Northumberland and Tameside for that day. Every one of the six new loans drawn in the year — £30m PWLB and £20m Market — was ≤1 year, driving the under-12-month bucket from 26.86% to 33.04%. Their explicit strategy is 'to minimise the taking on of long-term borrowing at elevated levels (>5%)' and focus on 'internal and temporary borrowing, supplemented by short-dated borrowing (<2 years)'. Paper explicitly ruled out rescheduling on a ~1% differential between new-borrowing and premature-repayment rates — do NOT contradict this; the £11.26m indicative net discount on the book is a separate observation about the position, not about the rescheduling arithmetic. Meeting has passed (15 July 2026); no next date printed.

summary.text:
The paper's own arithmetic is clean and the reconciliation is exact. Our file gives 44 PWLB loans totalling £138,905,254 at 3.9227% weighted; Appendix §3 (p.7) prints £138.9m at 3.92%. The five 31 March 2026 PWLB certainty rates it quotes on p.12 — 1yr 5.04%, 5yr 5.28%, 10yr 5.72%, 25yr 6.29%, 50yr 6.08% — all agree with our series to the basis point, the same set as Shropshire's Appendix A and consistent with Northumberland and Tameside for that day. The balance-sheet identity ties to the pound: CFR £255.0m − external £158.9m = £96.1m under-borrowing, exactly as printed (finance leases explicitly excluded on the CFR footnote, so no OLTL entry is needed).

The interesting shape is at the short end. Every one of the six new loans drawn in the year — £30m PWLB and £20m Market, £50m in total against a strategy assumption of £43m at 5.44% — was ≤1 year, at 4.29% to 4.45%. The under-12-month bucket has grown from 26.86% (£40.0m) to 33.04% (£52.5m); nearly 40% of debt reprices inside two years. This is deliberate: Appendix §4.2 says the Council has 'sought to minimise the taking on of long-term borrowing at elevated levels (>5%)' and focused on 'internal and temporary borrowing, supplemented by short-dated borrowing (<2 years) on a maturity loan structure'. The February drawdowns at 4.29-4.38% caught the short-end trough — the 1-year certainty rate rose to 5.04% by 31 March. The £10m December loan at 4.42% rolls this December against a today's 1-year of 4.95%.

Two things kept out of the email. First, the paper explicitly ruled out rescheduling in year on a ~1% differential between new-borrowing and premature-repayment rates; our engine's £11.26m net discount on the book is the position now, not the rescheduling arithmetic they modelled, and pushing back would read as an accusation. Second, the Audit Committee already sat on 15 July, so this is a between-meetings note rather than a pre-meeting one, and no officer email address is published in either document — the paper will need an address before sending.

officer.subject: Five printed rates matched, and £30m of PWLB drawn 1-year
officer.body:
Hi [FIRST NAME],

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are a few thoughts on the 2025/26 outturn that went to Audit on 15 July. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it. It's a well-scoped report, and this is offered in that spirit.

I want to start with something we owe the appendix, because it did us a favour twice over.

Appendix p.12 gives five PWLB certainty rates at the close of 31 March 2026 — 1yr 5.04%, 5yr 5.28%, 10yr 5.72%, 25yr 6.29%, 50yr 6.08% — and our own series gives all five for the same day, to the basis point. Shropshire's annual report prints the same five, and Northumberland's and Tameside's papers corroborate two of them. It's rare to find a run of five that ties across four councils. Then the debt-portfolio table on p.7 prints PWLB at £138.9m and a 3.92% weighted rate. Our file holds 44 PWLB loans at £138,905,254 and a weighted 3.9227%. That's exact on both. The balance-sheet identity ties too: £255.0m CFR less £158.9m external is £96.1m of under-borrowing, exactly as printed.

So this isn't a note about which way rates went. It's about the shape of what you've drawn.

Every one of the six new loans in the year was one year or shorter — three PWLB at £10m each (December at 4.42%, February at 4.38%, February at 4.29%) and three Market at £20m in total. That's £50m against a strategy assumption of £43m at 5.44%. Appendix §4.2 says why: 'sought to minimise the taking on of long-term borrowing at elevated levels (>5%)' and 'focused on a policy of internal and temporary borrowing, supplemented by short-dated borrowing (<2 years) on a maturity loan structure'. The February drawdowns at 4.29-4.38% caught the short-end trough — the 1-year certainty had risen to 5.04% by year-end. The under-12-month bucket grew from £40m (26.86%) to £52.5m (33.04%). It is a deliberate, coherent short-dated policy, running on a curve that hasn't reversed.

Today's 1-year certainty is 4.95%, 5-year 5.34%, 10-year 5.83%, 25-year 6.46%, 50-year 6.27%. Against your 31 March references the short end has drifted a touch lower and the long end a touch higher. The £10m December PWLB at 4.42% rolls in December against a 1-year that is 4.95% today; the February loans roll in February against whatever the 1-year is then. That's exactly the sort of thing worth watching weekly rather than at the next report, which is what the rates page at pwlbtoday.org/dashboard is for — both fixings, whole curve, ten seconds. We also hold all 44 of your PWLB loans at 31 March priced daily against the DMO repayment curve, so premiums and discounts are a lookup rather than a request: pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis. And the monthly sector breakdown is at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity — July was £368m across 33 loans from just 19 borrowers at an average 5.02%, which is a useful read on how thin the market is before you roll a £10m ticket.

One standing thing worth mentioning: our liability benchmark pathway is interactive and built on live data, which matters given where CIPFA is heading with the Prudential and Treasury Codes.

On training, three fit North Lincolnshire: Interest rate risk and Strategic PWLB borrowing, for the short-dated policy; and the liability benchmark pathway above. For members, Audit Committee Chair (Treasury) is written for exactly the committee this goes to. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts for the whole team.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
https://www.linkedin.com/in/russelltew

Source: Treasury Management Annual Report 2025/26 and Appendix 1 (Annual Treasury Management Review 2025/26), Audit Committee, 15 July 2026.
